In the Isolation Forest lecture, the professor mentioned **contamination** at **[21:29]** in the recording. 

He said: "In the demo I set contamination to 0.05, so the model flags the top five percent of points as anomalies. Set it too high and you start flagging normal data."

This means that the contamination parameter determines what percentage of data points are considered anomalies. Setting it to 0.05 (5%) flags the top 5% of points as anomalies, but setting it too high would cause the model to incorrectly identify normal data points as anomalies.

Source: [[Courses/CSCI 470/2026-11-06]]
